name: Thin native shell hosting the web client in WebView2
what: Teams desktop is a full-trust native Windows app (ms-teams.exe) that hosts the whole UI as a web client inside Microsoft Edge WebView2; the native layer owns windows, tray, toasts, updates, media, OS integration and crash recovery. If WebView2 is missing or too old the shell shows its own native error screen instead of the app.
how: AppxManifest declares Application MSTeams (Executable ms-teams.exe, Windows.FullTrustApplication) and an Optional external dependency Microsoft.WebView2 min 128.0.2739.67. The binary is C++ (vc143, C++/WinRT, WIL, Win2D, Boost 1.91, libcurl, sqlite3). Command-line token --embedded-browser-webview=1 and many msWebView2* experimental-feature names (TextureStream, EnableDraggableRegions, NativeEventDispatch, SimulateMemoryPressureWhenInactive, TerminateServiceWorkerWhenIdle...) show deep use of WebView2 controller APIs. Localized strings edge_not_installed_error, error_curtain_label_runtime_version_not_supported and download_edge_button_label cover the missing/outdated runtime case.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Frontend Plane is a SolidJS SPA plus Rust gateway; if a desktop client is ever wanted, the Teams split (thin native host, everything else web) is the low-cost path, with the native host owning only OS-level concerns.
notes: Peers: Slack and Grok Bot ship Electron; Teams moved to WebView2 (DOC-S: Tech Community post on the new architecture; page body not retrievable here). Evergreen WebView2 means the browser engine updates independently of Teams.

name: Bundled web client served from disk by the shell (local index)
what: The shell ships a copy of the web client inside the MSIX and serves it to WebView2 from disk, so first paint does not wait on the CDN; if the bundled build is older than a critical version, or the cloud does not support local index, it loads index and assets from the network instead.
how: A native WebAppLoader intercepts WebView2 WebResourceRequested for the statics endpoints (teams.microsoft.com/v2/statics etc.), maps network paths to local gzip files via desktop-assets/asset-manifest.json (fields networkPaths, localPath, content-encoding, cache-control), and injects response headers from serve-configs/<cloud>.json (CSP, Document-Isolation-Policy, Reporting-Endpoints) after substituting placeholders [[random]] (nonce), [[staticsPath]], [[rootUri]], [[containerName]], [[workload]], [[experienceName]], [[environment]], [[spoVanityDomains]]. maglev-configs/<cloud>.json gives rootUri, staticsUri, additionalStaticsUris and localIndexSupported (true for work, false for life/dod/etc.). Fallback reasons are logged as FromNetwork_LocalIndexNotSupportedForCloud, FromNetwork_ServiceWorkerUpdate, FromNetwork_ConsumerCloudMtma and 'Loading index from network since bundled version is too old ... critical version'. Responses carry header X-Ms-Maglev-Served-Asset. A WebClientVersionChecker reads package.json (@msteams/maglev-included-web-assets 260813193.14.50801226) and compares versions. ECS keys: webAppLoadingFromDisk, enforceLoadingOfBundledWebClient, checkWebClientVersion.
verevonRelevance: A bundled-assets-with-network-fallback loader gives instant start and a version floor; Verevon could adopt the same pattern if it wraps the SPA in a desktop host, and the placeholder-substituted per-environment CSP is a good model for its gateway.
notes: The local origin is virtual (hosts such as local.teams.microsoft.invalid appear in CSP and strings), not a real server. Most peers load the web app from the network or ship a fully local renderer.

name: Web assets updated as a separate package from the shell
what: The updater can refresh only the web-client assets (MicrosoftTeamsWebAssets) without replacing the native shell, so web fixes ship faster than full app updates.
how: ms-teamsupdate.exe strings: ': Attempting to update MicrosoftTeamsWebAssets', ': Failed to update web assets', 'Failed to register update package', 'Removing package'; ECS settings webAssetsLatestVersion, webAssetsBuildLink, latestVersion, dcatLatestVersion; shell ECS flag enableWebAssetsSupport. The AsyncBackgroundDownloader uses an allow list (downloaderAllowList, e.g. statics CDN hosts, authType none).
verevonRelevance: Separating the fast-moving UI bundle from the slow native host (and updating it through an allow-listed downloader) is directly applicable to a Verevon desktop shell.
notes: Exact package mechanism (MSIX optional/related package vs file drop) is not confirmed from strings alone; updater registers packages via Windows package APIs.

name: PIE: typed, versioned RPC bridge between web UI and native shell
what: The web client talks to native code through one uniform bridge (called PIE in the code) instead of ad-hoc IPC: promise-returning calls, host-to-web events, host-initiated calls, sync calls, and batching.
how: client-bindings/bundle.js defines HostBridge with message types InvokableSuccess, InvokableFailure, IdRequest, SyncFunction, Function, HostEvent; messages carry messageName, messageId, isInvokable, isIdRequest; batches use contentType 'app/piebatch' with a messages array; helpers: namespace version query (IdRequest 'version'), instance id, event forwarders, abandoned/timed-out call handlers, proxy forwarding, extended message properties, post-processors (Date, Pointer as Uint32Array pair, Uint8Array). Transport is WebView2: window.chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.piehostbridge (sync) plus postMessage JSON (async); window.pieSharedBridgeFactory shares one bridge across scripts; max message id 1073741823.
evidence: C:/Program Files/WindowsApps/MSTeams_26260.1701.5139.3736_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe/client-bindings/bundle.js:1 (token app/piebatch, class HostBridge, MessageType enum)
verevonRelevance: A single typed, namespaced, versioned RPC contract between UI and host is the cleanest way for Verevon to expose agent/host capabilities (browser grants, sandbox sessions, notifications) to the SolidJS UI without one-off channels; copy the namespace-version handshake and the batching.
notes: REA analyze_javascript_application on client-bindings (scout pass) was partial; findings here come from direct reading of the minified bundles. Provenance of REA coverage is stated in the deep dive.

name: PIE native-module catalog: 53 namespaces, ~545 methods and events
what: The shell exposes a broad, capability-per-module surface to the web client: auth, windows, toasts, taskbar, VDI, HID/Bluetooth, telemetry, updates, files, shortcuts, device discovery, recording detection and more.
how: bundle.js registers each namespace on globalThis.nativeModules (Airpods, Appdevicepermission, Auth, Bluetoothproximity, Brb, Callingcrosscloud(+persistent/transient), Core, Customvideobackground, Devicediscovery, Ecs, Etw, Fileopenpreference, Files, Fits, Gatt, Globalshortcuts, Heartbeat, Hfp, Hid, Hostcapabilities, Lastmiletelemetry, Logscollection, M365link, Moduleloader, Mtmahub, Noisesuppression, Ods, Officeintegration, Osutils, Platformapp, Profiler, Publicpreview, Recordingdetector, Roomservice, Scenario, Settings, Sharetarget, Spotlight, Taskbar, Teamsuseractivityrecall, Telemetry, Thirdpartydevices, Tmapolicy, Toasts, Updates, Userdataxcloud, Userpreferences, Vdi, Vdiconnectioninfoprocessor, Webclientstates, Windowcontrols). Largest: windowcontrols 65 endpoints, osutils 51, hid 38, core 34, vdi 25, toasts 24, mtmahub 21, telemetry 21, hfp 20, userdataxcloud 18. The native exe contains matching C++ classes (WindowControlsModule, ToastsModule, VDIModule ...) under msft::teams::native_modules.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a concrete checklist of host capabilities a mature chat shell ends up needing; Verevon should expose a much smaller subset (notifications, windows, deep links, auth handoff, updates, diagnostics) behind the same namespace pattern.
notes: Method names extracted with regex over invokeHost/registerForEvent literals; full list saved next to this file as teams.shell-and-native.pie-rpc-catalog.txt.

name: Sandboxed out-of-process native modules (remote modules)
what: Heavy or risky native modules, notably the SlimCore calling engine, can run in a separate low-privilege process so a crash or exploit does not take down the app window.
how: AppxManifest declares a second Application MSTeamsRemoteModuleContainer (same ms-teams.exe, Windows.PartialTrustApplication, uap10:TrustLevel appContainer, alias ms-teams_ac.exe). Strings: RemoteModuleFactory, ModuleLoaderServiceImpl (LoadRemoteModule, AddRemoteModuleToPie, HandleRemoteModuleEvent), named-pipe control channel ('Control Channel Created', 'Named Pipe Client created'), Job Object V1/V2 for remote modules, Sid::FromAppContainerName, ECS flags oopSlimcoreMode, oopSlimcorePrewarm, remoteModuleAppContainerEnabled, enableJobObjectForRemoteModules(V2), SlimcoreSandboxEnabled/Disabled, disableSlimcoreSandboxInVdi, enableSlimcoreRestartOnCrash, RemoteModuleCrash events. Remote modules plug into the same PIE namespace as in-process ones.
verevonRelevance: Strong template for Verevon's agent sandbox/browser sessions: run risky capability hosts out of process, in an AppContainer-like boundary, behind the same RPC namespace the UI already calls, with crash auto-restart and rehydration.
notes: Rehydration loop detection (enableSlimcoreRehydrationLoopDetection, maxSlimcoreRehydrationAttemptsPerTimeWindow) shows they hit restart storms in practice.

name: Reactive native core with cross-cloud stores
what: Inside the shell, state flows through observable streams and small redux-like stores rather than shared mutable objects, which keeps many windows, accounts and modules consistent.
how: RTTI names in ms-teams.exe show msft::teams::rx_internal (Subject, BehaviorSubject, Observable, AggregatedEvent), CrossCloudStore<..., variant<TeamsCloudCreated, TeamsCloudDestroyed, Set...Action>> with actions such as SetTransientStateAction, SetCloudProvisionedStateAction, AddProcessIdAction, SetLastHeartbeatDataAction, and event variants (WindowStateChangedEventArgs, WinToastActivated, NrcOwnerStateLoading/Error/Ready, CoreInitializedEvent, FirstPaintEvent, ExperienceWarmEvent, DesktopAppRestartEvent). Namespace counts: rx_internal 4349, native_modules 1787, win 1633, cross_cloud 1563, settings 922, slimcore 770.
verevonRelevance: Supports the idea that Verevon's desktop/host layer should be event-stream based with explicit state stores per account/space rather than imperative globals.
notes: Inferred from C++ type names only; no source available. Treat the 'redux-like' label as an interpretation.

name: Multi-account and multi-cloud shell (MTMA): one web instance per account
what: The user can be signed in to several work, school and personal accounts or guest tenants at once; the shell keeps each account's web client isolated while sharing calling state, notifications and a unified hub.
how: Native TeamsCloud objects (one per cloud/account) with TeamsCloudCreated/Destroyed events; PIE core.launchCloud, launchCloudByOpaqueId, getCloudCount, isMultiCloud, onCloudCountChanged, setUserContextIdOnWindow; ECS flags multiCloudLaunchEnabled, cloudRelaunchEnabled, tmaMultiCloudSupportEnabled, enableAsyncLaunchCloud, enableQueuingCloudLaunches, enableUseMostRecentCloudOnLaunch, enablePerCloudAutoStart; WebView2 storage partitioning per user context (ConfigureStoragePartition, 'Storage Partition: Auth Popup user context id', wv2ProfileEnabled); jump list items Add Another Account / Sign out from all accounts / Sign out of Active Account; web flags enableMTMA, enableMultiCloudAddAccount, enableCrossCloudLaunch, enableMTMATitlePrefix, enableMtmaHubInAppBar. DOC-S: Microsoft support article describes adding accounts via the profile menu with notifications from all accounts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has org rooms plus a personal Space; per-account isolated renderer/profile partitions plus a shared native hub is the proven way to support several orgs concurrently without re-login.
notes: Slack has workspace switching in one window; Teams keeps full per-account isolation and a native aggregation layer. MTMA expansion (multi-tenant multi-account) taken from DOC-S sources.

name: System tray with presence-aware icon and support actions
what: A tray icon shows the user's availability (and out-of-office variants) and offers Open, Settings, Auto-start toggle, My status, Sign out, Quit, plus support actions to collect logs and process dumps and to open dev tools.
how: desktop.json keys systray_menu_item_label_* (open, open_teams, quit, sign_out, settings, auto_start, do_not_auto_start, personal, close, log_support_collection, collect_dumps, open_dev_tools) and systray_tooltip_activity ('Microsoft Teams | New activity'); presence/system_tray/*.ico set (available, away, busy, dnd, offline and oof_* variants, context_menu_* icons, activity.ico); ECS flags showPresenceIconInNotificationIcon, dedicatedThreadForNotificationIcon, systrayIconCreateDelaySeconds, enableAutoStartMenu.
verevonRelevance: Basic tray with presence glyph and 'new activity' tooltip is table stakes; the built-in 'Collect Support Files' action is worth copying for supportability.
notes: Tray also exposes tooltip state for new activity.

name: Windows jump list: set status, new chat, calendar, upcoming events, accounts
what: Right-clicking the taskbar icon offers availability changes (Available, Busy, DND, Be right back, Appear away/offline, Reset), New Message, Open Calendar, Schedule Meeting, an 'Up next' list of today's meetings with join, and account actions.
how: desktop.json jumplist_menu_item_label_* and headers (Upcoming events, No upcoming events, All events, Up next, Tasks, Account, Add Another Account, Sign out/all/active); jumplist/*.ico incl. dark and high-contrast icons; command-line verbs --set-presence-to-available|away|be-right-back|busy|dnd|offline, --reset-presence executed by the running instance; ECS enableWindowsCustomizedJumplist, enableJumplistMeetings, enableJumplistChatLinkMeetings, enableJumplistCalendarLink, maxJumplistMeetings, enableJumplistQuit; PIE core.updateMeetingDetails/requestMeetingDetails feed meeting data to the shell.
verevonRelevance: Cheap, high-value OS surface: status changes and upcoming-work shortcuts from the taskbar; for Verevon the equivalent would be 'Ask agent', 'Open room', 'Pending approvals'.
notes: Implemented as command-line verbs, so no extra IPC channel is needed.

name: Taskbar integration: badges, flashing, pinning, avatar/presence icon
what: Unread/mention counts appear as a Windows taskbar badge, the taskbar button can flash, the icon can show the user's avatar and presence, and the app can pin itself.
how: WinMD Microsoft.Windows.BadgeNotifications.winmd shipped; PIE taskbar.showBadge/showBadgeAsync, setTaskbarFlashingSetting, getTeamsPinnedStatus (PinStatus enum: PinningNotSupported, TeamsConsumerAppNotPinned, TeamsForWorkAppPinned, PinningAllowedAndSupported, TeamsForLifeTrampoline), tryPinningTeamsApp, tryUninstallLegacyApp; StatusGlyph enum (activity, alarm, alert, attention, busy, error, oof*, available, away, doNotDisturb, offline, unknown); ECS enableTaskbar, enableAvatarTaskbarIcon, enableT22TaskbarPinningOverride, showAvailabilityInWindowsTaskbar, showUserInfoInWindowsTaskbar, enableTaskbarFlashIcon, enableLegacyBadge, enableDualBadgeService, enableMultiWorkCloudBadgeArbitration; strings FlashWindowEx logic that skips flashing when the window is foreground/active; web flags enableTaskbarBadgeMaglev, enableDirectMeetNowInWinTaskbarFlyout.
verevonRelevance: Unread badge plus 'arbitration' across accounts is the unread-management pattern Verevon lacks (no cross-room unread today).
notes: Badge arbitration across multiple work clouds is a nice detail: one badge number must be computed from several isolated web instances.

name: Auto-start manager with launch-count heuristics
what: Teams can start at sign-in, and it decides automatically: auto-enabled for frequent users, suppressed on low-memory or HDD devices, respectful of explicit user opt-out and group policy.
how: MSIX startup task TeamsTfwStartupTask via msteams_autostarter.exe plus an HKCU Run key path; states AutoStartEnabled, AutoStartDisabled, AutoStartDisabledByUser, AutoStartDisabledForLowSpecDevice, AutoStartDisabledForHDDDevice, AutoStartDisabledForTflApp; ECS autoEnableAutoStartEnabled, autoDisableAutoStartEnabled, launchCountToEnableAutoStart, numberOfPastHoursConsideredForLaunches, lowSpecDeviceMaxMemory, disableAutoStartOnHDDEnabled, preventAutoStartUntilUserInitiatedLaunchGroupPolicy, enablePerCloudAutoStart; telemetry shell_autostart_enable/disable; toast 'We've enabled auto start' with Disable button (desktop.json).
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships a desktop host, adopt a usage-driven auto-start with explicit consent toast and low-spec suppression instead of a blind default.
notes: Autostarter runs as a separate tiny exe (606 KB) so login cost is minimal.

name: Window close semantics: keep running, minimize on close, quit reasons, close prompts
what: Closing the window can hide, minimize, destroy, quit or ask first; the app can keep running in background, warn before leaving a call or discarding an unsent pop-out message, and remember the choice.
how: Native WindowCloseAction variant (Destroy, Hide, Minimize, ForceQuitApp, QuitApp, DoNothing, PromptDestroy) and WindowClosePrompt; PIE osutils.getKeepAppRunningOnClose/setKeepAppRunningOnClose, getOpenAppInBackground/setOpenAppInBackground, settings.getMinimizeMainWindowOnClose/setMinimizeMainWindowOnClose, windowcontrols.setClosePrompt/showClosePrompt/getClosePrompts (ClosePromptKey: Meeting, Send); strings closeprompt_meeting_* ('Leaving the call?'), closeprompt_send_* ('Your message hasn't been sent yet'), dont_show_again; ECS enableSpeedbumpsOnExit, enableRememberClosePrompt, allowCloseOverride, enableMinimizeMainWindowOnCloseSetting; DesktopAppStateChangeQuitReason has 17 reasons (EndSessionCloseApp, SystemTray, AppSwitcherInitiated, QuitOnCloseConfigured, DeeplinkQuit, JumpListQuit, SilentLaunchCompleted, RoomsIpcConnectionReceivedQuit ...).
verevonRelevance: The 'unsent message' and 'in a call' speed bumps are simple guard rails worth copying; recording quit reasons helps debug unexpected exits.

name: Window manager: tagged windows, persisted placement, named mutations, docking
what: Chats, channels, meetings, call monitors and presenter tools open in separate OS windows whose size, position and monitor are remembered per window type; windows can be hidden, docked or shown without activation by named rules.
how: PIE windowcontrols has 65 endpoints: mutateWindow, defineNamedMutations, dockWindow (DockSide Left/Right), getWindowByTag, hideAllWindows, hideWindowsIntersectingRect/unhideWindowsIntersectingRect, moveAfter, moveBy, setMinimumWindowSize, setWindowBounds(+ClientArea/Physical), setWindowAlwaysOnTop, flashFrame, key event hooks. Native window_placement_storage_* classes, window_cascade_impl, window_size_limiter_win; ECS enableMeetingWindowPlacementPersistence, enableChatWindowPlacementPersistence, enableChannelWindowPlacementPersistence, enableCallMonitorWindowPlacementPersistence, enableScreenTopologyPersistency (disabled in VDI/remote sessions), enableWindowIdPlacementPersistence, enableExternalWindowSync, unthrottledWindowTags.

notes: Placement persistence is keyed by window type and also by window id, plus screen topology memory.

name: Pop-out chats, channels and meetings with unsent-message protection
what: Any chat or channel can be popped into its own window; closing a pop-out with a message still sending warns the user, and meetings/calls use dedicated windows and a call monitor.
how: Shortcut command ids PopoutNewChat and PopoutConv; chatList_pop_out_new_chat_button_tooltip and embed_pop_out_chat keys; WindowTag ChatPopout/Meeting/Presenter; closeprompt_send_* for pop-out chats; ECS enableNonMainWindowInWindowedMode, enableCaptureOnNonMainWindow, disablePopOutMainWindow; web flags isCallingMultiWindowEnabled, enableCallingMultiWindowV2, enableContentPopout, contentPopOutLedLimit, enableDisposeMultiWindowIntentsForCrash.
verevonRelevance: Pop-out for a room or an agent run console is a likely requirement once users run several agents; plan state sharing between windows from day one.

name: Custom title bar, backdrop material and per-window frame themes

verevonRelevance: Accessibility-relevant (low-vision users); Verevon's SPA relies on browser zoom, which a desktop host must preserve.

name: Keyboard shortcuts: menu shortcuts, global hotkeys, custom assignment, mouse nav buttons
what: A catalog of named commands (new chat, pop-out, new meeting, join from toast, back history, chat filters, show shortcuts, report a problem) with menu-level and OS-global bindings, user-assignable custom shortcuts, and mouse back/forward button navigation.

name: Host command routing: entity types and actions shared by toasts, deep links and the hub
what: Activations from toasts, deep links and lifecycle events are normalized into (entity, action) commands that the web UI executes, so a click on a toast and a deep link take the same path.
how: PIE core.onExecuteCommand/executeCommand with HostCommandSource (toastFromWeb, toastFromHost, lifecycleEventFromHost), HostEntityType (calls, chats, toasts, signout, extensions, reminders, channels, activity, campaignnotifications, communities, callingdeeplink, communitiesevents, settingsstore, communitiesjoinrequest, communitiesmembers, alerts, notificationsdeeplink, files, chatrequests, meet, messagereminders), HostEntityAction (mutate, view, list, join, info, update) and LifecycleEventCode (Mounted, Dismissed, CriticalError, UserAction); core.intentHandled acknowledges.

name: Shell auto-update via background task, ECS-driven versions and idle restart
what: A separate updater app checks for new builds at start and periodically in the background (even when Teams is closed), downloads differential packages, stages them and applies on next restart, with an 'Update and restart' toast.
how: AppxManifest app MSTeams.Update (ms-teamsupdate.exe) with COM server args -RegisterComServerForUpdaterTask and -RegisterComServerForEcsTask; command-line -RegisterBackgroundUpdater, -CheckUpdate, -CheckUpdateAndForceRestart, -UpdateRestart, -BgTaskDelay, -EnsureTmaInstallation; BgUpdateCheck, BgUpdateRescheduleCount with min/max period and rescheduling multiplier/divider; ECS minUpdatePeriodMins, maxUpdatePeriodMins, maxAllowedUpdateDurationSecs, enableUnifiedUpdateScheduling, enableClientUpdateRestartSelf, disableUpdater; 'Auto update is disabled in VDI'; telemetry event shell_msix_update; the updater also fetches ECS before deciding ('Starting ecs fetch', EcsFetchCompletion). PIE updates.checkForUpdates/getHostUpdateState/hostUpdateEvents/tryInstallRestart/acquireNDIPackage. DOC-F (Learn, ms.date 2026-07-20): updates twice a month with staggered rollout, checks at launch and every few hours in the background, delivery via Windows Delivery Optimization with differential downloads, restart applies the update.
verevonRelevance: Verevon desktop would need the same tiers: staged background download, idle restart, ECS-style kill switches; it should also keep the update path independent of the running UI.
notes: Updates ride on MSIX, so Windows enforces file ACL integrity on WindowsApps (DOC-F warns that modifying the package breaks the app).

name: Update staleness gates: in-app nag, blocking page, update toast
what: Users on an old build see an in-app alert, and after roughly three months a blocking page that offers update, contact IT, or continue on the web.
how: DOC-F (Learn teams-client-update, ms.date 2026-07-20): alert when current version is one to three months old, blocking page beyond three months. Shell side: toast strings update_toast_title 'Update Teams', buttons 'Update and restart' and 'Remind me later'; ECS updateNotificationWaitTimeMin, updateNotificationExtendedWaitTimeMin, enableUpdateToastNotification; web 'checkWebClientVersion' and critical-version floor in the web loader.
verevonRelevance: A minimum-supported-client floor enforced server-side/with a blocking page protects protocol evolution; Verevon's gateway should expose a min-client-version contract if a desktop app exists.
notes: DOC-F for policy text; shell strings are SRC.

name: Native error curtain with diagnosis-specific messages and repair
what: When the web client cannot start, a native error screen explains the likely cause (certificate, proxy auth, policy, damaged package, low memory/disk, unsupported OS, outdated WebView2) and offers Restart, Repair Teams, or Open Teams on the web.
how: desktop.json error_curtain_label_*/body_* keys (generic, cert_info, proxy_info, policy_info, corrupt_package, resource_info, os_info, contact_it, runtime_version_not_supported), buttons error_curtain_restart_button, error_curtain_repair_teams_button, error_curtain_open_teams_on_the_web; native TeamsRepairManager, AppLaunchRepair, --repair-tool; ECS enableUserInitiatedRepair, enableTeamsRepair, enableLdsAppLaunchRepair, exitAppOnCoreWindowInitFailureEnabled, nativeLoadStateUxEnabled; basic-auth proxy dialog strings (basic_auth_dialog_*) when the proxy challenges.
verevonRelevance: Cause-specific failure screens with a web fallback and repair button are an excellent pattern for Verevon's own 'never go dark' contract at the client level.
notes: The curtain is native so it works even when WebView2 itself is the problem.

name: Renderer hang detection and recovery (Wait, Trace, Reload, Restart)
what: If the web process stops responding the shell shows a toast with Wait, Trace, Reload and Restart; it classifies process-failure kinds and can capture stacks.
how: desktop.json unresponsive_renderer_* strings; log 'mswebview2 renderer is likely unresponsive'; ProcessFailedKind enum (BrowserProcessExited, FrameRenderProcessExited, GpuProcessExited, RenderProcessExited, RenderProcessUnresponsive, SandboxHelperProcessExited, UtilityProcessExited, RemoteModuleCrashed); ECS numberOfUnresponsives, unresponsiveDurationSec, enableRendererUnresponsiveMultipleStackCollection, enablePrivateLoggerOnRendererUnresponsive, trackContentIdOfCrashedRenderer, disableRendererAmscQuarantine.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a checklist for client resilience (hang detection with user choice, process-failure taxonomy) if it embeds a browser engine.

name: Trouter: WebSocket push gateway (socket.io) with registrar service
what: Chat messages, presence updates, call invitations and other server events reach the client over one long-lived WebSocket to a service called Trouter, registered through a registrar; every cloud (commercial, gov, DoD, sovereign EU, China) has its own Trouter URL.
how: Web config keys trouterServiceUrl wss://go.trouter.teams.microsoft.com/v3/c and registrarServiceUrl https://teams.microsoft.com/registrar/prod/v2/registrations (config-life/config-prod chunks); per-cloud variants in web code (go.trouter.* for eaglex, scloud, sovcloud de/fr, dod, gov, china); the protocol library is socket.io (29 chunk hits). Flags: enableMessagingNotificationsOverTrouter=true, enablePresenceNotificationsOverTrouter=true, compressedTrouterPayloadPercentage=100, enableSynchronousTrouterResponse=true, enableTokenRevocationHandlingForCMDTrouter=true, trouterReRegistrationThrottleTimer=30, enableTrouterReRegistrationOnTokenRefresh=false, presencePostHeartbeatTrouterIntervalInMs=3600000. The native calling engine has its own Trouter client: SlimCorePIE TrouterOnTrouterConnected, TrouterOnTrouterDisconnected, TrouterOnTrouterMessageLoss, TrouterOnTrouterRequest, TrouterOnTrouterUserActivityStateAccepted, TrouterSendResponse, plus EngineHandlePushNotification/PushHandlingComplete and CallHandlerOnProxiedPushNotification.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's room updates are a 6 s poll; a registered push channel with explicit message-loss events and synchronous request/response over the socket is the proven design to remove that floor (see Verevon baseline: no push transport).
notes: Message-loss events imply gap detection and re-sync; payload compression is a flag, not default per cloud. Trouter is not publicly documented (DOC-S only via community writeups).

name: Client data layer (CDL) worker with GraphQL/Apollo ForestRun cache
what: Data fetching, caching and updates for chats, channels and calls run in a dedicated worker (the central data layer), exposed to the UI as GraphQL with per-feature resolvers and a partitioned normalized cache, so the main thread stays responsive.
how: Native client-agent signals central_data_layer_worker_manager_startup and central_data_layer_data_store_create; web workers manifest 'cdlWorkerManifest' with six inner worker bundles (services_i, defer-loaded, b, c, d, f); trusted-types policies @msteams/core-cdl-worker-common#create-cdl-worker. Flags (config-prod): isCDLWorkerCriticalToStartup=true, enableSupermassiveCDL=true, enableBatchedCDLUpdates=true, failAllGraphQLIfCDLFailed=false, enableApolloForestRun=true, enableApolloForestRunPartitions=true, enableApolloDataEviction=true, maxApolloCacheOperationCount=500, apolloForestRunPartition* operation counts, enableGraphQLStoreStatsReporterService, cdlMultiContextColumns, calling CDL event throttle rates (callingCdlParticipantsChangedEventThrottleRate, callingCdlVoiceLevelThrottleRate, callingCdlStartStreamsBatchRate). enableSharedWorker is false in this build, so the dedicated-worker path is the default; a SharedWorker build exists (precompiled-shared-worker).
verevonRelevance: Moving normalized-cache and server sync into a worker behind GraphQL-style resolvers is a strong target architecture for Verevon's SolidJS client once it has threads, runs and approvals to cache; pair it with the offline queue below.
notes: CDL is expanded as 'central data layer' in native strings; the web-side name is 'CDL worker'. Apollo ForestRun is a Microsoft-developed Apollo cache implementation (flag names only; implementation not inspected).

name: Offline action queue with guaranteed ordering for send, delete and read-state
what: Messages sent or deleted while offline are queued, kept for up to 48 hours, retried across sessions, and replayed in order; read position updates are also offline-capable.
how: Web config (prod): offlineSupportedResolvers=[sendMessage, setConsumptionHorizon, undeleteMessage, deleteMessage]; offlineGuaranteedOrderingEnabledResolvers=[sendMessage, undeleteMessage, deleteMessage]; offlineActionsManagerDefaultActionExpirationInMs=172800000 (48 h); offlineActionsManagerDefaultCrossSessionRetries=10; offlineActionsSyncStrategyRefreshIntervalInMs=600000 (10 min); related flags enableOptimisticCreate, enableResponsiveOptimisticStatePrediction, enableRaiseHandsOptimisticResponse, enableOfflineCallingAuth, enableRetryScreenForOfflineCcCode. Native side feeds connectivity via osutils.getNetworkStatus/networkStatusChanged.
verevonRelevance: Verevon explicitly has no offline cache or queued send because each message needs a fresh content-bound Control decision; the Teams numbers (48 h TTL, 10 retries, per-resolver ordering) show what a queue needs, and Verevon would need a 'deferred decision' design for it.
notes: Only four mutations are offline-capable; everything else fails fast. Ordering is guaranteed only for message-state mutations.

verevonRelevance: When wrapping a web app in a host, replace the service-worker cache with host-managed asset serving to avoid two competing caches.

name: Cross-window and cross-worker state via BroadcastChannel, batching and Web Locks

name: Cross-cloud global state stores and consistency resync between native and web
what: With several accounts, the shell keeps a global view of user data, calling state and missed notifications, pushes it to every web instance, and periodically verifies the web side matches (consistency check and resync).
how: PIE modules userdataxcloud (18 endpoints: setUserAccountData, setUserAuthStateData, setUserPresenceData, setUserProfileData, setUserProfilePictureData, setUserTenantsData, setMissedNotificationsForUser, getGlobalUserData, onGlobalUserDataChange, onSecureGlobalUserDataChange, deleteUserAccount, postStateForConsistencyCheck, AuthConsistencyCheckEvent, ConsistencyResyncEvent), callingcrosscloud(+persistent/transient) (get/setPersistentState, setTransientState, onGlobalPersistentStateChange; CoordinatedStates defaultState, stateRequested, stateConfirmed, stateRejected, stateInitiated), mtmahub. Native CrossCloudStore with actions; ECS enableConsistencyResync, consistencyCheckTimerInSeconds, consistencyCheckEnabledTypes (ConsistencyItemType AuthState, MissedNotifications). Persistent call keys include selected speaker/microphone/camera devices, noise suppression mode, spatial audio, E911 location consent.
verevonRelevance: A native-owned global store with explicit consistency checks and 'state requested/confirmed/rejected' handshakes is a robust way to share read/unread, presence and device choices across rooms or accounts; Verevon lacks any cross-room aggregate today.
notes: The 'secure' global user data channel suggests token-bearing data is kept off the normal channel.

name: Shell-side settings and state persistence with atomic writes and migration
what: The shell stores its own state in small JSON files (preferences, app and cloud settings, window placements, account lists, ECS caches), writes them safely, and migrates legacy settings.
how: File names in ms-teams.exe: client_preferences.json, app_settings.json, cloud_settings.json, cmd_settings.json, tma_settings.json (active_users/primary_users account lists), app_switcher_settings.json and tfl_app_switcher_settings.json, window_placements, vdi_connection_info.json, webview_prelaunch_args.json, previous_session_data.json, crash_reports_cache.json, ecs_settings.dat, tma_ecs_settings.dat, lds_override.json, auth_account_migration.json, consumer_settings_migration.json, skype_migration.json; ECS swapFileWriterEnabled (atomic replace), enableClientPreferencesFilter, TeamsSharedConfig publisher cache folder shared across Microsoft apps; WebView2 profile folder 'EBWebView'; per-profile log root.
verevonRelevance: Atomic settings writes and explicit migration files are a small but important host hygiene point.

name: Native media transport stack: ICE, DTLS-SRTP, RTP with RED/RTX/NACK, dual DTLS (Rust or OpenSSL)
what: Calls run on a native stack with ICE connectivity, SRTP media, FEC/RED and retransmission, and a DTLS handshake implemented either in Rust (DTLS 1.2 and 1.3) or OpenSSL.
how: skypert.dll exposes CreateDtlsEndpointDimpl (Rust crate dimpl 0.7.2, source paths dtls12 and dtls13) and CreateDtlsEndpointOpenssl (OpenSSL 3.0.18 statem_dtls.c), CreateDTLSPipe for SCTP data channels and SRTPProfile selection; ic3rustcore.dll exports dimpl_dtls_create/handle_packet/handle_timeout/keying_material/srtp_profile/protocol_version and uses Windows BCrypt for X25519, AES-GCM, AES-CCM-8, ChaCha20-Poly1305 (DTLS 1.3 test vectors present). RtmMediaManager has SDP parser/session/media, ICE server and DNS cache; RTMPLTFM has rtpsend/rtprecv/rtpred/rtpsec/rtpstats/rtpdtmf and SRTP primitives; codec strings include Opus, SILK, G722, G729, PCMU/PCMA, AMR, Siren, SATIN, H264, H265, AV1, SLIQ, RTX, NACK, transport-cc, telephone-event, with FEC and congestion/probing terms in RTMPLTFM.
verevonRelevance: Not Verevon's problem near-term, but if agents join calls as participants the media security baseline (DTLS-SRTP, modern ciphers) is the bar; Rust DTLS plus a selectable fallback is a migration pattern.
notes: Strings identify implementations, not which path runs by default.

name: WebSocket and endpoint inventory enforced by CSP (Trouter, Substrate, Augloop, PPT Live, eCDN, speech)
what: The set of real-time services the client may open sockets to is explicit in the served CSP: push (Trouter), Substrate signals, Augloop collaboration, PowerPoint Live, attendee/webinar services, eCDN peers, cloud speech/captions, voice and biometrics, plus localhost debug sockets.
how: serve-configs/work.json default endpoint connect-src (44 entries) includes wss://*.trouter.teams.microsoft.com, *.trouter.gcc..., *.trouter-df..., wss://substrate.office.com, wss://*.augloop.office.com and svc.cloud.microsoft variants, wss://*.pptservicescast.officeapps.live.com, wss://*.attend.teams.microsoft.com/.net/cloud.microsoft, wss://*.cts.speech.microsoft.com (captions/transcription), wss://*.enterprisevoice.svc.cloud.microsoft, wss://biometricsvc.teams.cloud.microsoft, wss://*.ecdn.teams.microsoft.com, wss://*.peer5.skype.net, wss://*.svc.ms, plus development targets ws://localhost:*, wss://127.0.0.1:9002, http://localhost:4318 (OTLP), wss://view-localhost:*. A templated form wss://{appliance_fqdn}:4444/v3/c also appears in web chunks (purpose not stated; possibly a customer-hosted or on-premises appliance variant).
verevonRelevance: An explicit allow-list per realtime service, per cloud, is how Verevon's gateway should expose room push, agent progress and collaboration without a wildcard connect-src.
notes: The endpoint list reveals product architecture: separate services for captions, attendee view, biometrics and eCDN rather than one realtime bus.

name: PIE tunneled over VDI virtual channels (Citrix, Horizon/Omnissa, AVD, AWS DCV)
what: In virtual desktops the same SlimCore JSON-RPC runs between the web client in the VM and the media engine on the user's endpoint, carried over the vendor's virtual channel, so one API serves local and remote media.
how: vdibridge_wv2.dll (VM side, WebView2) has DetectVendor, CommProtocolHandler, ScreenScraperInterface, 'ClientDownloadingSlimCore', Omnissa transport, AWS DCV virtual channel APIs (DcvWtsApi.dll), Citrix receiver thread; JS bundles scpie_vdi_bridge, scpie_vdi_sc and scpie_vdi_webrr reuse window.pieSharedBridgeFactory and expose V8Bridge_ToHost/ToHostSync/GetStartingSyncId/SetFromHostCallback; contentType 'app/webrr' messages carry remote-message events for WebRR; SLIMCORE_VERSION constant '2026.36.1.6'; web flags enableSlimCorePieVdiService(+MTMA), enableDynamicLoadingForScPieVdiBundleAndBridge, pieVdiBridgeReportingIntervalInMinutes, enableDeferredSlimCorePieVdiServiceInit.
verevonRelevance: A single RPC contract reused across in-proc, out-of-proc and remote transports is the model for Verevon sandbox/browser sessions that may run on different hosts than the UI.
notes: DOC-F (Learn VDI page, updated 2026-10-01) confirms the new SlimCore-based optimization is the default with WebRTC redirection being retired for Windows endpoints.

name: End-to-end encryption plumbing for calls and meetings
what: Calls and meetings can be end-to-end encrypted with a client-version floor, a data channel for key exchange, E2EE status events, and clear 'not allowed under E2EE' rejections for server-side features; chat is not covered.
how: Calling bundle: ECS SkypeCalling/enableDataChannelForE2EE default true, isE2EE state, onE2EEncryptionStatusChanged, enableE2EEncryption, TransactionNotAllowedForE2EE errors and operation tag NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_E2EE; web flags enableE2EEMeetings=true, enableE2EEV2=true, e2eeMinSlimcoreVersion=2021.14, e2eeMeetingMinSlimcoreVersion=2022.40, e2eeOptOut, enableE2EEChatBanner, e2eeMiddleTierEndpoint; SlimCore API CallHandlerOnE2EEncryptionStatusChanged. DOC-S (Learn teams-encryption snippet): one-to-one E2EE is opt-in by admin and user, meetings need Teams Premium and organizer opt-in, keys via GKMP over TLS 1.3 for meetings, AES-256-GCM media, recording/transcription/recap unavailable under E2EE.
verevonRelevance: Documents the cost of E2EE (no recording, recap, transcript); Verevon agents need plaintext access, so E2EE rooms must exclude agents or be an explicit mode.
notes: DOC-S via search snippet; Learn page not fetched in full.

name: Memory-aware app caching with LRU eviction in the web shell
what: The web client keeps recently used apps/tabs warm and evicts them by least-recently-used when device free memory is low, with a larger floor on some platforms.
how: Web flags: enableAppCachingMemoryMonitoringNS (platform-conditional), cachedAppMemoryEvictionStrategyNS=LeastRecentlyUsed, appCachingFreeMemoryMinMegabytesNS=1024 (512 for platform code 50), appCachingTotalMemoryMinMegabytesNS, appPrecachingMemoryReductionPerAppMegabytes, enableAppCachingMemoryTimeline, platformAppMemoryHeartbeatSharedAppList; shell supplies memory info through osutils.getSystemMemoryInfo and heartbeat metrics.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon keeps several rooms or agent consoles mounted, adopt a memory-budgeted LRU rather than unbounded caching.

name: Multi-device identity and push registration
what: Each device and endpoint has an id and registration so the service can route pushes and calls to the right device, including mobile registration through Substrate.
how: Binary tokens TeamsDeviceId in skypert, RtmMediaManager and SlimCoreWebview2; SlimCore EngineGetRegistrationId/EngineRegisterUser/EngineReregisterContextsEx2; x-ms-endpoint-id header; substrate.office.com/UserDeviceGraphService/user/mobile-registration endpoint in the exe; ECS enableLoggingGlobalDeviceId and logEntraDeviceIdInTelemetry; Windows push via Microsoft.Windows.PushNotifications.winmd and background tasks (UniversalBGTask).
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs a device/endpoint registry owned by Control (not the browser) before any push or multi-device read state can work.

name: Scalability levers: batching, throttling and 'supermassive' tenant mode
what: Large tenants and busy calls are handled by batching and throttling update streams (participants-changed events, voice levels, CDL updates) and a dedicated large-scale CDL mode.
how: Web flags enableSupermassiveCDL=true, enableBatchedCDLUpdates=true, callingCdlParticipantsChangedEventThrottleRate, callingCdlVoiceLevelThrottleRate, callingCdlStartStreamsBatchRate, filterCallingCDLEventsByDiffing, SkypeCalling enableParticipantsEventsBatching and enableOptimizedSpeakerChangeEvents, inMemoryCleanupBatchSize; shell side sideTraffic throttling and PIE message batching (app/piebatch).
verevonRelevance: Plan batching and diffing for agent progress streams early; per-event updates will not scale with many agents.

name: Network state, proxy and connectivity handling
what: The shell tracks connectivity and Wi-Fi, handles proxy basic-auth challenges with a native dialog, and the web client has a network detector and retry UX.
how: PIE osutils.getNetworkStatus/networkStatusChanged/getFilteredWifiInfo; ECS enableNetworkStatusTracker, enableNetworkDetector (telemetry SDK), enableBasicAuthDialog, basicAuthRequestMaxBatchSize, basicAuthRequestBatchTimerMs, useSystemProxyForUpload, disableHttp2, enableLocalNetworkAccessChecks; desktop.json basic_auth_dialog_* and connectivity_error_secondary_text; error curtain text for proxy and certificate errors; web errors namespace has chatsync_app_service_disconnected (scout inventory).
verevonRelevance: Corporate proxy auth is a real deployment issue; Verevon's gateway/BFF avoids it for browsers, but a desktop host would need the same dialog.

name: Native Windows toast service with categories, image cache and dismissal reasons
what: Notifications are real Windows toasts activated through a COM callback, with registered categories, cached images, per-toast style, and precise knowledge of why a toast was suppressed or dismissed (disabled by policy, disabled by user, Focus Assist, timeout).
how: AppxManifest toastNotificationActivation CLSID 816EB0E0-F985-4919-BDA3-315878A4ED80 (ms-teams.exe ExeServer). Native ToastServiceWin, ToastActivatorWin, CreateToast, ToastCategory registration ('ToastCategory not registered'), ToastImageCache, 'Toast data too big' guard, WinToastActivationCallback::Activate (with NOTIFICATION_USER_INPUT_DATA for reply-style inputs), DismissToast, telemetry Toast.DismissalReason/FailedReason/UserNotificationState. Enums: NotificationState (DisabledByGroupPolicy, DisabledByManifest, DisabledForApplication, DisabledForUser, Enabled), ToastDismissalReason (UserCancelled, ApplicationHidden, TimedOut, FocusAssist), ToastFailure (Unknown, NotificationDisabled, NotificationTypeDisabled), ToastButtonStyle (success, critical). Log text maps WPN_E_NOTIFICATION_DISABLED to 'Windows notifications are disabled for the Teams app'. PIE toasts.requestNotificationAuthorization, getGlobalNotificationSettingsAsync, getWebNotificationSettings, removeNotificationByKey.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no notifications at all; a toast service that knows why a toast failed (policy vs user vs focus mode) is the minimum for trustworthy 'agent needs approval' alerts.
notes: Slack and Teams both use native toasts; Teams' categorized registration plus failure taxonomy is more complete.

name: Custom in-app notification panel: position, density, collections, content protection
what: Besides OS toasts, Teams can render its own toast window (a notifications panel) in any screen corner, in compact or comfortable density, with grouped notification collections, timed auto-hide, and protection from screen capture.
how: PIE toasts: createCollection/removeCollection/collectionActivated, getToastWindowPosition/setToastWindowPosition (ToastWindowPosition BR, BL, TL, TR), setToastSizeThemeSetting (ToastSizeTheme Compact, Comfy), setToastDisplayTimeSetting, offsetNotificationsPanel/resizeNotificationsPanel/getAvailablePanelHeight, setNotificationsPanelContentProtection; log 'creating notifications panel'; ECS enableNotificationsWindowFourCornerPositioning, enableVisualHostingForNotifications (composition visual hosting), autohideToastTimeout, disableCustomMSNToast, toasts/enableMacLiquidGlass (Mac variant), enableNotificationsWindowMacOcclusionMovement; web flags enableInAppToasts(V2), enableBannersAsToasts, enableInteractionRequiredToast, enableUpdatingCallToasts (toast content updates in place), enableCQUpdatableToast.
verevonRelevance: A host-drawn toast with grouping, density setting and in-place updates is the right surface for live agent progress ('Verevon is working...') that OS toasts cannot update.
notes: Capture-protection of the panel avoids leaking message previews during screen sharing.

name: Focus Assist and presence-aware notification suppression
what: Toasts respect Windows Focus Assist/quiet modes (priority only, alarms only) and Teams presence, and the client tells the user when a toast was dropped because of Focus Assist.
how: PIE toasts.getFocusAssistStateAsync/focusSessionChanged/notificationModeChanged with FocusAssistState (AlarmsOnly, Off, PriorityOnly) and ToastNotificationMode (Unrestricted, PriorityOnly, AlarmsOnly); native GetFocusAssistState, UserNotificationState, 'Public NotificationMode API is unavailable on Windows SV3 or higher', 'Toast dismissed with TimedOut reason can be caused by Focus Assist'; ECS focusAndNotificationModeObserverEnabled, minWindowsBuildForNotificationModeObserver; web flag enableHonoringPresenceForNotification; presence DND mapping through the status model.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs DND/quiet-mode semantics before adding push; reading OS focus state and explaining dropped notifications avoids silent failures.
notes: Windows later removed the public notification-mode API on newer builds; Teams has a fallback path.

name: Cross-account missed-activity hub with consistency-checked counters
what: The shell aggregates missed chats, channel messages and activity across all signed-in accounts into one hub (used by the tray/hub UI and badges), with per-tenant pin status and filters.
how: PIE mtmahub (21 endpoints): setHubActivityFeed, setHubFolders, setHubSliceContent, setHubTenantData/updateHubTenantData, setHubTenantPinStatus, setHubContentFilter, updateHubMissedNotifications/Chat/Channel/ActivityNotifications, onReceiveHubNavigationRequest/onReceiveHubActivityNavigateRequest, postStateForConsistencyCheck; trusted counterpart mtmahubtrusted (getGlobalFlattenedHubData, submitTrustedHubNavigationRequest). Hub model enums: HubContentSurface (ACTIVITIES, CHATS, TEAMS_CHANNELS, SLICE), HubFeedBadgeType, HubNavTargetKind (CHAT, CHANNEL, COMMUNITY, CALL, DEEPLINK, COMMAND, COMPANION), HubNavigationErrorCode (INVALID_REQUEST, ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, AUTH_REQUIRED, UNSUPPORTED_TARGET, TARGET_UNAVAILABLE, EVENT_RAISE_FAILED, TIMEOUT), HubAuthState (Up, InteractionRequired, AADReconnecting, SkypeReconnecting, LicenseError, SignInRestriction, UnRedeemed, LoginError, OnTenantPicker, RestartDevice); ECS mtma consistency checks; web flags enableMtmaHubInAppBar, enableMTMANotificationsMainWindow. Trusted UI chunks mtma-hub-page-view and mtma-missed-notifications render it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's missing 'cross-room unread aggregate' is exactly this; publishing a compact, typed unread/attention projection from the web layer to a trusted host surface keeps counts correct across rooms/orgs.
notes: The hub is rendered by the Trusted UI (locked-down page) rather than the full web client.

name: Notification signal classes and cross-cloud toast settings
what: Notifications are typed by signal (call, mention, chat, channel, other, consumer-community) and each cloud/account can have its own toast settings, with a cross-cloud setting for which accounts may alert.
how: NotificationSignal enum (call, mention, chat, channel, other, lifeCommunity); PIE toasts.getCrossCloudToastSettings/crossCloudToastSettingChanged; userdataxcloud.setMissedNotificationsForUser; ECS disableCustomMSNToast; per-cloud badge arbitration (enableMultiWorkCloudBadgeArbitration). DOC-S (Microsoft support): notifications are on by default for organizations joined as a guest and can be managed in settings.
verevonRelevance: A small closed set of signal classes makes mute/DND/routing rules manageable; Verevon should classify attention events (mention, approval, agent result, run failure) the same way.

name: Notification sounds, ringtones and secondary ringer device
what: 24 bundled sounds cover ringing, meetup rings, screen-share rings and notification tones; the app can ring on a second audio device and use Teams sounds instead of OS alert sounds.
how: Audio/ folder with ring.mp3, ringring.mp3, incoming-ringtone-level30/40.mp3, meetup_ring.mp3, screenshare_ring.mp3, teams_notification.mp3, teams_meet_up_reminder.mp3 and 16 selectable notification tones (beep, bop, bounce, bubbles, plink, ripple, wobble ...); shell SetNotificationSoundsIntent and fixForToastCallSounds; persistent call state key callingSelectedSecondaryRingerDevice; SlimCore AudioPlayerStartAudio/AudioPlayerOnEvent; evergreen asset https://statics.teams.cdn.office.net/evergreen-assets/audio/Teams_Call_Ringing.mp3.
verevonRelevance: Distinct sounds per urgency class (call vs reminder vs mention) matter once agents can interrupt people.

name: Windows push and background wake-up for calls and updates
what: The app can be woken for incoming calls or updates when not running: Windows push, background tasks, an autostarter, and push handling inside the calling engine.
how: WinMD shipped: Microsoft.Windows.PushNotifications, ApplicationModel.Background (+UniversalBGTask), AppLifecycle; SlimCore EngineHandlePushNotification/EnginePushHandlingComplete, CallHandlerOnProxiedPushNotification/OnIncomingProxiedMessages; background updater tasks (-RegisterBackgroundUpdater, BgTaskNotSupported); startup task and Run key; voipCall/phoneCall capabilities in the manifest.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs a push path that works when the tab or app is closed; plan device registration, a push gateway under Control authority, and ZDR-safe payloads (no content).
notes: Exact push service (WNS) and payload shape are not visible statically.

name: In-app banners and call toasts in the web layer
what: The web client has its own toast/banner system for in-context alerts (scam suspected in call, emergency group call toast, newly created group call, decorated caller names, interaction required).
how: Web config flags: enableInAppToastsV2, enableBannersAsToasts, enableInteractionRequiredToast, enableScamSuspectedInCallToast, enableNewlyCreatedChatGroupCallToast, enableFixForEmergencyGroupCallToast, enableDecoratedToastCallerName, enableCallRedirectionToastForPA, enableCallToastCallerDisplayNameLessStrictPhoneFormatCheckRegex, enableZoomToast (56 toast-related keys in config-prod).
verevonRelevance: Distinguish 'in-context banner' from 'OS toast' in Verevon's attention model.

name: Presence model with out-of-office variants, hourly heartbeat over push, and OS-surface control
what: Availability (Available, Busy, Do not disturb, Be right back, Away, Offline, reset) has out-of-office variants, is set from the tray, jump list or command line, is kept alive by a heartbeat, and is shared with Office apps.
how: AvailabilityType enum (available, busy, doNotDisturb, beRightBack, away, offLine, resetAvailability); HubPresenceAvailability; presence icon set with oof* variants; command-line --set-presence-to-* and --reset-presence; core.updateAvailabilityOnNative/userAvailabilityChanged; officeintegration.notifyPresence/trackPresence/untrackPresence to Outlook/Office through the IM provider; web flags presencePostHeartbeatTrouterIntervalInMs=3600000, enablePresenceNotificationsOverTrouter=true, enableUsersPresencePrefetch, disablePresenceForMeetings, enablePresenceStatusTaskbar, disableAgenticUserPresence (agent users may have presence).
verevonRelevance: Verevon presence is room-scoped; a global status with DND plus agent presence (see agentic-user flags) is the next step, and OS surfaces can set it cheaply.

name: Link-preview unfurling for crawler user agents
what: Teams links shared in other chat apps can unfurl: the served web app whitelists known preview-bot user agents so social/chat crawlers get metadata.
how: serve-configs/work.json supportedUserAgentsRegexPatterns includes SkypeUriPreview, Slackbot-LinkExpanding, facebookexternalhit, ChimeUnfurlAgent, DingTalkBot-LinkService, Snap URL Preview Service, kakaotalk-scrap, Iframely, WhatsApp, URSA; supportedBrowsers min versions: Edge/Chromium 97, Firefox 101, Safari 16.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon room/run links are pasted into Slack or Teams, an unfurl-safe preview endpoint (with ZDR-aware minimal metadata) improves hand-off.

name: Message slices: all messages, mentions, tag mentions, threads, drafts, saved, reminders, VIP, requests
what: The client models attention-worthy message views as typed slices (including VIP and priority, tag mentions, reminders with upcoming/due/completed states, drafts, saved) usable in the hub and feeds.
how: HubSliceType (ALL_MESSAGES, DISCOVER, DRAFTS, MENTIONS, MENTIONS_GROUP, REMINDERS, REPLIES, REQUESTS, SAVED, TAG_MENTIONS, VIP, UNKNOWN); HubSliceIdType with _CHAT/_CHANNEL splits for mentions, group mentions, threads, saved, drafts, priority, requests, all messages, vip, reminders; HubSliceCardKind; HubSliceChatModality (POSTREPLY, CONVERSATIONAL, UNTHREADED, SESSIONS); HubSliceGridLayoutType (DIRECT_MESSAGE, GROUP_CHAT, CHANNEL_POST, CHANNEL_REPLY, CHAT_REPLY, MESSAGE_CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE); HubSliceReminderStatus (UPCOMING, DUE, COMPLETED); HubChatSubType (ONE_ON_ONE, SELF, GROUP, MEETING, BOT, NEW_CHAT).
verevonRelevance: A fixed slice taxonomy (mentions, drafts, saved, reminders, requests, VIP) gives Verevon a ready backlog for 'needs my attention' views beyond the Activity tab; note it includes SESSIONS chat modality for bot sessions.
notes: Slack calls similar views Activity, Saved, Later and Drafts; Teams adds VIP and tag mentions.

name: SlimCore: native media engine API (call control, merge, park, transfer, nudge, bot sessions)
what: A native engine, SlimCore, runs calls and meetings behind a large API: join/leave, mute for everyone, admit from lobby, consultative transfer, call park/unpark, merge, call-me-back, nudge, place to voicemail, add participants, meeting layout and roles, bot session start, live-interpretation attributes, spatial audio positions and E2EE status events.
how: scwv2_bundle.js exposes 434 SlimCorePIE/Hid2PIE/BttPIE/NativeHost endpoints; CallHandler* alone has 124 (e.g. CallHandlerJoinMeetingGroup, JoinPreheatedCall, AdmitParticipants, CallMuteParticipants, StartConsultativeCallTransfer, StartCallPark, MergeCallParticipants, NudgeParticipants, CallMeBack, PlaceCallToVoicemail, StartSessionWithBot, SetLiveInterpretationAttributes, UpdateParticipantInterpretationState, SetMeetingLayout, SetParticipantSpatialAudioPositions, StartInRoomFaceAtrribution, ProvideCallQualityFeedback, PublishState/RemoveState); events for active/dominant speaker lists, remote video count, audio stream state, E2EE status, batch operation status. Other groups: MediaStreamSession* (preheated sessions, feed views), ContentSharing*, StageController*, DataChannel*, Compositor*, VideoReceiver*, FrameSink*. SLIMCORE_VERSION 2026.36.1.6. The calling JS layer (calling_electron_bundle.js, @skype/skype-calling-electron) wraps it with ECS flags under SkypeCalling and SkypeVideoLibrary.
verevonRelevance: The breadth (park, merge, nudge, bot sessions, publish-state) shows what 'agents in calls' will eventually need; start with bot sessions and state publication, not media.
notes: The 'bot session' and 'interpretation' APIs are the media-plane hooks for agents and AI interpreters (see agents category).

name: Screen sharing pipeline with scraper, sharing indicator, annotation and remote control injection
what: Screen and window sharing uses native capture (Windows Graphics Capture with GDI fallback in sandbox), a sharing indicator, annotation, PowerPoint slide transition info, and a control injector that lets another participant move slides or take remote control.
how: ssScreenVVS2.dll with ECS flags VBSS_EnableGdiFallbackInSandbox, VBSS_PauseCaptureOnWindowMinimize, VBSS_UseOcclusionManagerPrintWindow, VBSS_ScraperRestartMaxRetries, VBSS_GraphicsCaptureAccessCheckTimeoutMs, VBSS_EnableExtendedScraperEvents; SlimCore VideoBindingScreenShareScraperEvent, ScreenShareGetCurrentSharingInfo, ScreenShareGetPPTTransitionInfo, ScreenShareSetAnnotationWindow, SharingIndicatorSetPosition/SetWindow/SetToolbarWindow, ControlInjector (AllowSingleController, InjectRawmInput, InjectSlideMove, SetAvatar, SetCursorConfig, SetInjectionRect), ContentSharingTakeControl; manifest capabilities graphicsCapture, graphicsCaptureProgrammatic, graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder; shell ECS enableVMSSMaxFps, enableVMSSMaxResolution, enableAppSharingControl; SlimCore EngineEnableShellSharing/EngineDisableShellSharing/EngineUpdateShellSharingWindowId.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to agent 'computer use' in rooms: a human-visible sharing indicator, a single-controller rule and an injector with an explicit allowed rectangle are the safety UX to copy.
notes: Remote control is constrained to one controller (AllowSingleController) and a rectangle.

name: Local meeting recording on the client
what: The client can record a meeting locally (screen/window region, optional system audio) to a user-chosen folder, independent of cloud recording.
how: SlimCore LocalRecordingStart/Stop/IncludeSystemAudio/SetCaptureRegionAndWindow/GetCaptureRegionAndWindow/RelinkToBinding/OnError, EngineGetLocalRecordingSessions/GetOrCreateLocalRecordingSessionInfo; ECS SkypeVideoLibrary/enableLocalRecording; PIE userpreferences.GetLocalRecordingLocation/ChangeLocalRecordingLocation, files.openLocalRecordingFolder; web flag bypassLocalRecordingPolicy=false.
verevonRelevance: Local recording bypasses server compliance recording, which is why Teams also ships external-recording detection (see governance); Verevon must decide whether agents may record.

name: NDI output: virtual devices, on-demand package download
what: Participant streams can be exposed as NDI video sources for production tools; the NDI runtime is downloaded on demand as a signed package.
how: SlimCore NdiCreateVirtualDevice/DestroyVirtualDevice/UpdateParticipantStream/UpdateSettings/IsSupported/DevicesChangedEvent/SendToDevice; ndiDownloadUrlTemplate https://teams.microsoft.com/core-calling-lib/{version}/ndi-win-{arch}_vs2022-crtdynamic-release.msix; PIE updates.acquireNDIPackage with NDIPackageStatusState (Success, AlreadyInstalled, FailedDownload, FailedVerification, FailedRegistration); ECS enableGeneralPackageManagementNDI; localized ndi_auto_* strings.
verevonRelevance: Shows the pattern of keeping heavy or licensed runtimes out of the base package and fetching them verified on demand; useful for optional agent runtimes.

name: On-device ML for audio and video with cloud-delivered models and safe fallbacks
what: Noise suppression, echo cancellation and video segmentation run on-device via ONNX/WinML; models are downloaded from the cloud and each stage falls back to a classic algorithm if ML fails or the device is too weak.
how: onnxruntime.dll (8.4 MB) shipped; RTMPLTFM strings: ADSP_DeepNS_ProcessSamples, ADSP_TFNet_ONNX_ProcessSamples, ADSP_DeepAEC_Config_SetOnnxIntraOpThreadPoolSize with messages 'Switching to Skype noise suppressor' / 'classic noise suppressor'; ECS ADSP_VQE_UseOnnxForTFNet and DeepAEC thread settings; 'AiCloudClient provides functionality to download ML models'; 'Device capability ML model ...' metrics with a Low/Mid/High band; FrameProcessingInferenceEngine (FPIE) DnnSession; SlimCV has CreateSlimSegmentation, CreateVideoSegmentation, CreateFaceTrackerML, CreateBlurProcessor, beautifier segmentation, LoadModelArchive; SlimCore EngineDownloadAiModel/ModelDownloadComplete; ECS EnableDNNChromaKey.
verevonRelevance: Device-capability-gated, cloud-delivered, fallback-safe model use is a good template for Verevon's local inference ideas (e.g. on-device redaction before upload).

name: Camera and background features: auto-framing, PTZ, manual controls, custom backgrounds, AI cameras

name: Package integrity and signing of the shell (MSIX) as a tamper boundary
what: The app is distributed as a signed MSIX with a block map; Windows protects files under WindowsApps and treats modified files as corruption, and the app shows a 'damaged installation' screen.
how: AppxSignature.p7x, AppxBlockMap.xml, AppxMetadata/CodeIntegrity.cat, CodeSignSummary-*.md signing logs; error_curtain_body_corrupt_package; DOC-F (Learn updates page): modifying ACLs/files under Program Files/WindowsApps makes Windows treat the package as corrupted and breaks updates.
verevonRelevance: Signed package plus OS-enforced immutability is a stronger tamper boundary than a self-updating exe in user space.

name: Third-party devices and apps API: local WebSocket server with pairing and meeting commands
what: Teams runs a local WebSocket server on 127.0.0.1 so hardware and apps (such as Stream Deck plug-ins) can read meeting state (muted, hand raised, in meeting, recording, permissions) and send commands (mute, camera, hand, blur, reactions, leave) after the user allows pairing; admins and users can disable it.
how: Native ThirdPartyDevicesManager/Impl using Boost.Beast WebSocket on loopback (StartServerAndListen, CloseServer, SendMeetingUpdateMessageToAllClients, HandleDevicePairingStatusUpdate, HandleTpdAppPreferenceUpdate); messages carry fields manufacturer (1-40 chars), device, appName, pairingStatus, meetingState, meetingPermissions, isMuted, isHandRaised, isInMeeting, isRecordingOn, canToggleMute, tokenRefresh; blocked clients receive nothing; server not started if disabled by app preference or policy; PIE thirdpartydevices (getDevicesList, isThirdPartyDevicesServiceEnabled, onThirdPartyDevicesRequest, onThirdPartyDevicesPairingRequest, sendMeetingUpdate, sendPairingStatusUpdate, sendPolicyUpdate, sendResponse, sendErrorResponse, sendAppPrefUpdate) with MeetingAction (queryMeetingStateV2, mute, unmute, toggleMute, showVideo, hideVideo, toggleVideo, raiseHand, lowerHand, toggleHand, blurBackground, unblurBackground, toggleBackgroundBlur, leaveCall, sendReaction, toggleUi, stopSharing, pair) and PairingStatus (allowed, blocked, unpaired). DOC-F (Microsoft support): admin policy must allow it; pairing prompt Allow/Block when joining a meeting; token generated in Privacy settings; Allowed/Blocked lists with Forget. DOC-S (community docs): default port 8124 with token query parameter.
verevonRelevance: A loopback, token-paired, allow/block-listed control API is the right pattern for letting local agents or hardware drive a Verevon desktop host with explicit user approval and admin kill switch.
notes: Tokens are per client and refreshable; commands are rejected until pairing completes. Port number not recoverable from strings (stored numerically).

name: Office/Outlook integration: IM provider registration, presence COM server and UC type library
what: Teams registers as the instant-messaging provider for Office so Outlook and other apps can show presence and start chats or calls via a COM server and a large automation type library.
how: AppxManifest COM ExeServer 'Office Integration' (CLSID 88435F68-FFC1-445F-8EDF-EF78B84BA1C7) and a type library registration with 299 COM interfaces (x64/uc.tlb, x86/ucx86.tlb, arm64); command-line --register-im-provider, -InitializeMSTeamsIMProvider, -UnsetMSTeamsAsDefaultIMProvider, -SetMSTeamsUpAndRunning{Starting,Started,Stopped}; registry SOFTWARE/IM Providers/MsTeams; PIE officeintegration (registerIMProvider, isRegisteredIMProvider, startComServer, stopComServer, trackPresence, untrackPresence, notifyPresence, startChat, startCall, logStatement); ECS enableSfbIpcCommunication for Skype for Business coexistence; type library identifiers cover conversation, contact, conference, participant, endpoint, modality, sharing, channel, meeting, presence, status, notification, subscription, search, device, history.
verevonRelevance: OS/app-suite integration (presence in Outlook, click-to-chat) is a distribution moat Verevon lacks; a smaller automation surface (open room, post to room, presence) via protocol handlers would cover most value.
notes: The 299-interface count is from the manifest comInterface entries.

name: Outlook Teams Meeting Add-in (TMA) installer and coexistence policy modes
what: The package carries the Outlook meeting add-in installer and policy modes for coexistence with Skype for Business (islands, Skype-only, Teams-only), controlling which meeting provider Outlook offers.
how: MicrosoftTeamsMeetingAddinInstaller.msi (15.7 MB) in the package root; updater commands -EnsureTmaInstallation and 'Attempting to install or update meeting addin'; ECS enableMeetingAddinMsiDrop, tmaSettingsEnabled, tmaMultiCloudSupportEnabled; settings tma_settings.json; PIE tmapolicy.setTeamsMeetingAddinPolicies with TeamsUpgradePolicyMode (Islands, IslandsWithTempInterop, IslandsWithVoipDeepLinking, SfBOnly, SfBWithTeamsCollab, SfBWithTeamsCollabAndMeetings, TeamsOnly, Legacy) and MeetingProviderForIslandsMode (TeamsAndSfb, Teams); shipped config flag tma/meetingAddinEnableVirtualAppointment=false.
verevonRelevance: Calendar-originated meeting creation is where users meet Teams; Verevon's agent-meeting use cases (Meeting Scribe) would need an equivalent calendar add-in or link handler.

name: Windows AI actions: Chat and Schedule actions registered with the OS
what: Teams registers two Windows AI actions (send a message, schedule a meeting) for a contact so Windows can surface 'Send a message with Teams' next to email addresses; both are shipped unavailable and non-generative in this build.
how: AppxManifest windows.appExtension com.microsoft.windows.ai.actions Id MSTeamsActions with PublicFolder desktop-assets and Registration action_manifest.json (version 2): MSTeams.Action.Chat (Uri action-sip:${contact.Email}) and MSTeams.Action.Schedule (action-schedule:${contact.Email}), inputs of kind Contact, where clause non-empty email, isAvailable false, usesGenerativeAI false; protocols action-sip and action-schedule registered; strings send_message_action and schedule_meeting_action.
verevonRelevance: OS-level actions are an emerging entry point for agents; Verevon could register 'Ask Verevon' style actions via a protocol plus manifest when a desktop host exists.
notes: Feature is dark in this build (isAvailable false).

name: Share target: send files, text and images to Teams from any Windows app
what: Teams appears in the Windows share sheet and accepts any file type, text and bitmaps; shared files are made available to the web client through a virtual path.
how: AppxManifest windows.shareTarget 'Send to Microsoft Teams' (SupportsAnyFileType; StorageItems, Text, Bitmap); PIE sharetarget.getSharedFiles; native ShareSessionManager; ECS enableShareTarget and sharedFilesWebInterceptablePath (served as https://local.teams.microsoft.invalid/shared-files/ through WebView2 request interception).
verevonRelevance: Share-target is the cheapest way to let people drop content into a Space from anywhere; map it to a Control-authorized upload to the room.

name: Dynamic native module loading and host-capability negotiation for the web client
what: The web client can ask the shell whether a native module exists, load or unload it at runtime, and learn the host's capabilities (and updates to them), so the same web build works across hosts (Windows, Mac, VDI, Rooms).
how: PIE moduleloader (hasModule, loadModule, unloadModule, moduleStatusEvent) and trusted moduleloadertrusted; native ModuleLoaderServiceImpl creating remote (out-of-process) modules and 'Unload failed due to module not being out of proc'; hostcapabilities (getCapabilities, getInitialCapabilities, onCapabilitiesUpdated) with HostCapabilitiesImpl flags such as IsThirdPartyDevicesManagerEnabled; web flag enableDynamicLoadingForScPieVdiBundleAndBridge.
verevonRelevance: Capability negotiation plus lazy module loading is the extension model Verevon should adopt for per-room agent tools and sandbox hosts: the UI asks 'what can this host do' and loads only what is allowed.

name: Platform-app hosting hooks: app lifecycle state, origin allow-lists, optional browser extensions
what: The shell knows the lifecycle of embedded platform (tab/meeting) apps, throttles or exempts them, restricts which hosts they may navigate to, and can load browser extensions in dev scenarios.
how: PIE platformapp.setPlatformAppInfo with PlatformAppState (Cached, Active); ECS unthrottledPlatformAppIds, platformAppMemoryHeartbeatSharedAppList, allowedTopLevelHosts, allowedHostNames, pptLiveOrigins, enableSensitivityLabelForPlatformApps, enableExtensions, command-line --load-extension; web chunks platform-app-*, platform-app-deeplink-to-sidepanel-execute (scout inventory).
verevonRelevance: If Verevon hosts third-party agent UIs, give the host a lifecycle API (cached vs active) and per-app origin allow-lists.

name: Xbox Game Bar widget package update hook
what: Teams ships or updates a Game Bar widget package, extending meeting controls to the Windows overlay.
how: ECS flag enableTeamsGameBarWidgetMSIXUpdate and enableGenericPackageModularInstaller in the shell; updater package registration code paths. No widget UI strings were recovered.
verevonRelevance: Marginal; indicates the modular package installer pattern for optional OS-integrated extensions.
notes: Low confidence: names only.

name: Agentic users: agent identities treated as users with presence, roster and call-button controls (dark by default)
what: The client has flags to treat AI agents as first-class 'agentic users': onboarding, listing in manage-apps, optional presence, call button, and filtering them from @mentions, rosters and thread member lists; in this build the master flag is off and agent presence is disabled.

verevonRelevance: Confirms Microsoft is moving to agents as roster members with their own identity and (optionally) presence plus a distinct avatar shape; Verevon already lists agents in the Members tab, but lacks presence and a human-vs-agent visual language.
notes: Flag names and defaults only; behaviour not observed. 'Squircle' styling suggests agents get a different avatar shape.

name: Bot streaming, stop button, ephemeral messages, delivery reports and AI controls in channels
what: Bots/agents can stream replies, users get a Stop button, bots can send ephemeral (visible-to-one) messages, delivery reports show message status, and channel AI controls let moderators manage bot AI behaviour; these are on by default in this build.
how: Config-prod: enableBotStreaming=true, enableBotStreamingStopButton=true, enableBotStreamingRegulator=false, enableBotEphemeralMessages=true, enableBotDeliveryReports=true, enableBotAIControlsInChannels=true, enableBotsInRoster=true, enableBotSessionsTypingIndicator=false, plus enableBotSessions*/BotSessionsChatUnwrapping/BotSessionEventHandling (session-style bot chats; HubSliceChatModality SESSIONS), enableBotConfiguration, enableBotZeroPrompts, enableBotDynamicCommandsSyncEngine, enableBotCardActionFederationCheck, enableBotComplianceDialog (off).
verevonRelevance: Streaming with a Stop button matches Verevon's SSE stream plus cancelInvocation; ephemeral messages and delivery reports are good fits for approvals and 'agent posted for you' receipts.
notes: The regulator flag (off) suggests rate-shaping streamed edits; internals unknown.

name: Meeting-artifact access through an MCP service (MCPS) for agents
what: The client reads meeting artifacts (recordings, transcripts, recap sources, podcasts) via a Model Context Protocol-style service and exposes tool details, enabling agents to consume meeting content.
how: Web config: enableMCPMeetingArtifacts=true, enableMCPToolsDetails=false, enableGetMeetingListByMcps, enableGetPodcastByMcps, enableTranscriptV2MCPDownload, enableTranscriptV2MCPFlow, meetingTypesForMCPSContentsAPI, useExternalIdForMCPSContentsAPI, regionalMCPSEndpointPath, regionalMCPSListArtifactsByUserEndpointPath, regionalMCPSPodcastsEndpointPath, cmdMCPSEndpoint, enableMCPSAsP1RecapSource, enableMCPSForMeetingDetailsRecordingTile, botsAllowedForMcpWidget, enableMessagePreviewForChatCitationInMCP. notes: Interpretation of MCPS as an MCP server/service name is an inference from key names.

what: Agent management UX is being built: agent details page with permission view and reviews, blueprint-based creation from the store, interaction prompts, per-app permissions, sync after agent creation, and support in shared channels; most are off in this build's defaults.

name: Agents in meetings: bot sessions, interpretation state and meeting-bar subscriptions
what: At the media layer, bots can start sessions, AI interpretation attributes and per-participant interpretation state can be set, and personal or pinned agents can subscribe to the meeting bar (flagged off here).
how: SlimCore CallHandlerStartSessionWithBot, SetLiveInterpretationAttributes, UpdateParticipantInterpretationState, StartInRoomFaceAtrribution/StopInRoomFaceAtrribution; web flags enablePersonalAgentSubscriptionInMeetingUbar=false, enableAgentPinSubscriptionInMeetingUbar=false, enableAiInterpretationTurnByTurnModeSpeakerBadge; Teams SDK/Agents SDK documentation is covered in the scout inventory.

what: The main executable declares per-monitor-v2 DPI awareness, the segment heap allocator and normal (non-elevated) execution, and disables window filtering so capture/enumeration sees all windows.
how: Embedded RT_MANIFEST (2,453 bytes, located with REA inspect_pe_resources which examined 867 resource entries): dpiAware true, dpiAwareness PerMonitorV2, disableWindowFiltering true, heapType SegmentHeap, requestedExecutionLevel asInvoker uiAccess false, Common-Controls 6.0, Win2D activatable classes, supportedOS Windows 10/11 with maxversiontested 10.0.26100.0, description 'Microsoft Teams (work or school)'. A Limited Access Feature IDENTITY resource (64 bytes) is also present (value not recorded).
evidence: REA evidence ev_63833651ee3b0554fd6b81f5960d8a6518e70463edc3f8387a031b6054768a67 (inspect_pe_resources ms-teams.exe: 431 resources, 867 entries, complete)

name: Public-preview / ring opt-in handled by the shell with next-launch semantics

how: Strings and ECS: convergence, convergenceAndT2Installed/NotInstalled, convergenceDownloadLinkX64/X86/Arm64, isAppQuitFromT22Enabled, enableT22TaskbarPinningOverride, usePreInstalledT22Threshold, migrateNonActiveT20WithNoT21, uninstallT20WebFlowKillSwitch, avoidInstallingT22WithRoomsClient, TflAppSwitcherInitiated quit reason, app_switcher_settings.json and tfl_app_switcher_settings.json (defaultApp), AppSwitcherSettingsChecker/EnsureAppSwitcherSettings, GetStartPageFromIntentOrT22Migration, shell_app_switcher_migration telemetry, -T22PinningOverride; start-page flags for consumerStartPageUrl and startWithWorkUser. name: Multi-architecture distribution (x64, arm64, x86) and per-arch type libraries
what: Teams ships for x64, ARM64 and x86; the package carries per-architecture COM type libraries and the admin docs link per-arch MSIX downloads.
how: Package folders x64/uc.tlb, arm64/uc-arm64.tlb, x86/ucx86.tlb; this package is the x64 build (ProcessorArchitecture x64); DOC-F (Learn VDI page) lists MSIX x86, x64 and ARM64 downloads and the teamsbootstrapper.exe provisioning path; convergence download links per architecture (ECS).
