name: Meeting entry points from OS surfaces: jump list, toast join, taskbar Meet Now, Outlook, tel/sip/callto
what: Users can start or join meetings and calls without opening the app window: from the jump list's upcoming events, a toast Join button, a taskbar Meet Now/Schedule flyout, Outlook add-in, and tel:/sip:/callto: links.
how: ShortcutCommandId JoinMeetingFromToast and CalendarNewMeeting; jump list upcoming events fed by core.updateMeetingDetails/requestMeetingDetails (MeetingState Accepted, Tentative, Declined, NotResponded); web flags enableMeetNowInWinTaskbarFlyout, enableDirectMeetNowInWinTaskbarFlyout, enableScheduleMeetingInWinTaskbarFlyout; WindowTag MeetNow; protocols tel, sip, sips, callto, action-schedule; TMA installer; strings jumplist_menu_item_label_not_teams_meeting ('Not a Teams meeting' tooltip for events without a link).
verevonRelevance: Reducing clicks to start an agent-assisted meeting from the OS (jump list or protocol link) is cheap value for Verevon Meeting Scribe flows.

name: Audio device routing: preferred output devices, device manager and selected-device signals
what: The shell has an audio output device manager, passes the selected speaker to the media layer and uses browser preferred-output-device support (via origin trial) so web audio follows the user's choice.
how: WebViewWindowWin takes an AudioOutputDeviceManager; PIE userpreferences.SignalSelectedAudioOutputDeviceChanged; ECS enablePreferredAudioOutputDevices; index.html carries origin-trial tokens for the PreferredAudioOutputDevices feature on teams.microsoft.com and teams.cloud.microsoft; persistent keys callingSelectedSpeakerDevice, callingSelectedMicrophoneDevice, callingSelectedSecondaryRingerDevice; SlimCore RtcAudioHandlerSetAudioConfig, EngineStartAudioLoopbackDevice, loopback/shared system-audio driver install flows (osutils.startSharedSystemAudioDriverInstalation, getBundledSystemAudioDriverVersion).
verevonRelevance: Voice agents will need output-device selection and optional system-audio capture; note the shared system audio driver install as a heavy dependency for sharing sound.
notes: System-audio sharing uses an installed loopback driver, not just OS APIs.

name: SlimCore lifecycle: preemptive load, versioned load/unload, retry and rehydration after crash or sleep
what: The calling engine is loaded early (preemptive check), can be disposed and re-initialized, retried on failure and rehydrated after crash, lock or sleep, with loop detection to stop restart storms.
how: Web flags (config-life/prod) enablePreemptiveCallingServiceLoadCheck, preemptiveCallingServiceLoadCheckTimeoutInSecs=20, enableSlimCoreLoadV2, enableSlimCoreUnloadV2, enableSlimCoreInstanceDisposeAndReinit, enableSlimCoreOperationRetry, slimCoreOperationRetryIntervalsInMs=[3000], enableTsCallingPackagePrefetch, getCallingApiTimeoutInMs=10000, slimCoreStackTelemetryStepAllowListForCSI; shell enableSlimcoreRestartOnCrash, enableSlimcoreRehydrationLoopDetection, maxSlimcoreRehydrationAttemptsPerTimeWindow, enableSlimcoreHostServices, updater telemetry AppInfo.SlimcoreRehydrationCount; web enableSetSlimCorePieStateOnMachineLocked; SessionStatus Locked/Unlocked/Resumed/Suspending events.
verevonRelevance: Treat long-lived capability hosts (browser, sandbox, media) as restartable with rehydration and a restart budget, as Teams does.

name: Read state: throttled mark-as-read, optimistic 'client lie', read receipts and unread navigation
what: Marking messages read is optimistic on the client and rate-limited on the network (max three concurrent calls per eight seconds), with read receipts and unread-thread navigation shortcuts; the read position (consumption horizon) is one of the few mutations queued offline.
how: Web config: markAsReadAPIThrottleRate {maxConcurrentCallsCount:3, throttleLimitTimeQuantum:8000}, enableMarkAsReadNetworkCallThrottling=true, enableMarkAsReadRetryPolicy=false, enableActivityMarkAsReadClientLie=true (client reflects read before server confirms), enableMarkAllAsReadLogic, enableActivityMarkAllAsRead, enableReadReceipts=true, enableUnreadThreadNavigationShortcut, offlineSupportedResolvers includes setConsumptionHorizon; shortcut command SeeUnreadChats.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's server-side read marker works across devices; adding optimistic client marking plus throttled/queued updates would make unread feel instant without hammering Convex.
notes: Retry policy for mark-as-read is off by default, so failures rely on later sync.

name: On-demand message and channel translation with language hints

verevonRelevance: Verevon's Norwegian/English mix suggests on-demand translation as a room feature; pass language hints as headers and keep it ZDR-safe (no retained translations).

name: Tenant awareness in a multi-org client: pin tenants, title prefixes, tenant rendering across clouds
what: Users can pin tenants in the hub, window titles can carry an organization prefix, and tenant data is rendered across clouds so people always know which organization context they are in.
how: PIE mtmahub.setHubTenantPinStatus/setHubTenantData/updateHubTenantData and trusted setTrustedHubTenantPinStatus; userdataxcloud.setUserTenantsData; web flags enableMTMATitlePrefix, enableRenderingCrossCloudTenant, enableMTMARemountOnRootProvider, enableOnIdleForMTMA, initializeMTMAModeOnStartup; strings tenant picker (auth_tenant_picker_header, from the scout inventory).
verevonRelevance: Always-visible org context (title prefix, pinned orgs) is a safety UX that Verevon's org-vs-personal Space switch should adopt to prevent posting in the wrong context.

name: Mini-mode compact window and minimized call view (dark by default)
what: A compact 'mini' window with its own counter badge and prewarm, plus a minimized view for calls, exist as a lightweight always-available surface; they are disabled in the shipped defaults.
how: WindowTag Mini; web flags enableMinimodeWindow=false, enableMinimodePrewarm=false, enableMinimodeCounterBadge=false, enableMinimizedViewForCalls=false, enableSISUOnMiniMode; shell minimumSupportedWebClientVersionForMiniWindow and enableMinimalWindow / msWebView2EnableMinimalWindow (WebView2 minimal window mode).
verevonRelevance: A compact quick-reply or agent-status mini window is a candidate Verevon surface once a desktop host exists.

name: First-party Copilot surfaces hosted as separate origins in the shell
what: The shell recognizes dedicated Copilot web origins (a Teams-hosted Copilot app and Microsoft 365 Copilot chat/app services, plus a local development host) and treats Copilot processes as a Medium-risk AI assistant in recording detection.
how: ms-teams.exe strings: https://copilot.teams.cloud.microsoft, https://local.copilot.teams.office.com, https://m365copilotchat.svc.cloud.microsoft, https://m365copilotapp.svc.cloud.microsoft, m365copilotapp; allowed-origin handling via allowedTopLevelHosts/allowedHostNames; recording-detector entries copilot, M365Copilot, mscopilot (appType AIAssistant, risk Medium).
verevonRelevance: First-party agents get their own origin and CSP rather than sharing the main app origin; Verevon should host agent-rendered UIs on isolated origins.
notes: Low confidence on how the origins are embedded; only host strings were recovered.

name: Schema-agnostic native layer: opaque state blobs and opaque ids across the bridge
what: The shell stores and forwards some web-defined state (hub data, user data, login flows, cloud ids) as opaque payloads it does not parse, so the web client can change schemas without shipping a new native build.
how: PIE endpoints getOpaqueGlobalHubData/onOpaqueGlobalHubDataChange (mtmahub), getOpaqueGlobalUserData/onOpaqueGlobalUserDataChange (userdataxcloud), launchCloudByOpaqueId (core), enum OpaqueAuthenticationAccountType; ECS opaqueEnabled, disableOpaqueLoginFlows, disableReplaceOpaqueInSetLoggedOutStateData; alongside typed enums for the parts native does need (auth state, availability, window tags). Each generated PIE module also exports GetPIEScriptVersion (value 1) and JsonPostProcessing helpers.
verevonRelevance: Keeping the native host thin and schema-agnostic where possible lets Verevon's web UI evolve independently; type only what the host must enforce (auth, window, notification, permission).
notes: Design interpretation of the 'opaque' naming; the payload formats are not visible.

name: PII-aware native and JS logging bindings with encryption and report-a-problem upload
what: Native and JavaScript logs share one logging layer that classifies fields as safe or unsafe for PII, can write encrypted or unencrypted logs, and feeds the report-a-problem upload.
how: client-bindings/rt_js_bindings_bundle.js (@skype/rt-js-bindings) exposes RootToolsManager, logInSClog, writeLogData, jsLogFileConfiguration, setBRBCallback and uploadBRB; strings show classifications Unsafe, Inherited_Unsafe, Inherited_Safe, Blacklisted_Unsafe, encryption modes Encrypted/Unencrypted/Compress, levels Fatal to Debug6, component, thread and timestamp fields, ULOG2 and ULBaseline log types; ECS RootTools/SC_EphemeralReleaseEnabled; shell enableLogSanitizer(+SanitizationMode), piiLoggingEnabled, DebugPii severity in LogSeverity (debugPii, debug, info, warning, error); log-collection exclusions per locale (localesExcludedForLogCollection).
verevonRelevance: Per-field PII classification in the logging API (not post-hoc scrubbing) supports Verevon's ZDR and audit needs; adopt a 'debugPii' tier that is compiled out of production.
notes: Bundle is a thin binding over a native RootTools logging core.

name: Biometric and face-profile service endpoints isolated behind a dedicated socket origin
what: Face and biometric enrollment features talk to a dedicated biometrics service and are modelled as separate, consented flows with export and delete options.
how: CSP connect-src wss://biometricsvc.teams.cloud.microsoft in serve-configs; lazy app chunk biometric-enrollment and locale strings recognition_export_biometrics_button_text, recognition_create_profile_button_text_v3 (scout inventory); SlimCore StartFaceStream/StopFaceStream and StartInRoomFaceAtrribution for in-room attribution; voice signature storage via PIE noisesuppression (separate consent). Admin controls are tenant-side (not visible here).
verevonRelevance: Biometric features need their own service boundary, consent and export/erase; Verevon should refuse to mix voice/face data into room history or agent memory by default.
notes: Depth of tenant controls and retention not visible from the client.

name: Scheduled send with recipient working-hours delivery suggestions
what: The compose flow can suggest a delivery time based on the recipient's working hours (scheduled message delivery), with a cached working-hours lookup; the suggestion flag is off in this build's defaults.
how: Web config keys: enableScheduleSendSuggestionsHeimdall=false, scheduledMessageDeliverySuggestionWorkingHoursCacheLengthSeconds=259200 (3 days), disableScheduledMessageDeliverySuggestionWorkingHoursCache=false, enableWorkingHoursInLPC (working hours on the profile card). The scout inventory could not confirm scheduled send from locale keys; these flags show a scheduled-message delivery path exists server- and client-side.
verevonRelevance: Scheduled send plus working-hours awareness is a natural fit for agents that should deliver summaries at a sensible time; Verevon's schedule primitives (cron runs) could post into rooms at recipient-friendly times.

name: Hybrid push plus poll with relaxed intervals under push and lock-aware presence polling
what: Even with a push channel the client keeps polling as a safety net, but relaxes intervals when push is healthy and stops polling presence while the machine is locked; presence is polled when the machine becomes active again with a throttle.
how: Config-prod: calendarEventsPollIntervalInMs=90000 versus calendarEventsPollIntervalWithPushInMs=180000, enablePollSubscribedPresenceOnActive=true with pollSubscribedPresenceOnActiveThrottleInMs=120000, disablePollPresenceOnMachineLocked=true, presence heartbeat over Trouter hourly, enableDropLongpollMessagesFromReadThreads=false (a legacy long-poll message path still exists); shell supplies SessionStatus Locked/Unlocked/Resumed/Suspending (PIE osutils.sessionStateChanged) and native signal cdl_startup_sync_conversation_list_on_machine_active to re-sync on wake.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's 6 s visible-tab poll could adopt the same shape: keep polling as a fallback but back off to a long interval once a push channel is attached, pause on lock/hidden, and force a re-sync on resume.
notes: Shows Teams treats push as an optimization over polling, not a replacement, which also simplifies recovery after message loss.
